origin.description: Format strings with printf specifiers, recycled over every argument.
origin.usage: stri_sprintf(format, ..., na_string = NA_character_, inf_string = "Inf", nan_string = "NaN", use_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: A character vector of format strings.

arguments.name: na_string
arguments.text: Text used for a missing value. NA keeps the output missing.

arguments.name: use_length
arguments.text: If TRUE, string width counts code points. If FALSE, it counts columns.

origin.details: Supported specifiers are dioxX, feEgGaA, and s, including flags, width, precision, and positional arguments. A double passed to %s is formatted with as.character. A missing format element makes that output missing.

translation.description: Format strings with printf specifiers, recycled over every argument.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: A format string, or a list of them.

arguments.name: *args
arguments.text: Values for the specifiers. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: na_string
arguments.text: Text used for a missing value. NA keeps the output missing.

arguments.name: use_length
arguments.text: If True, string width counts code points. If False, it uses stri_width.

translation.details: Finite numbers are formatted with libc snprintf. %s of a double uses R's as.character, so 1e5 prints as 1e+05 and 1e-4 prints as 1e-04. NA stays missing when na_string is NA. The string "NA" is text.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing element is NA.
